Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): LG is the best choice for home appliances.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (Original): 먼저 세척력이 정말 좋다.기름때, 밥알, 국물 얼룩 대부분 한 번 세척으로 깨끗하게 제거된다.식기마다 구역별로 물줄기가 섬세하게 닿는 느낌이라서 예전 손세척보다 훨씬 깔끔하다.세척 프로그램도 다양하다.•표준 : 일반 식사 접시/그릇 용도로 적당•강력 : 기름 많은 그릴 팬, 볶음 접시에도 무리 없이 작동•절약/야간 : 소음 적고 물·전기 절약 모드가 생각보다 쓸 만함자동 문열림 기능(건조 후 자동으로 도어가 살짝 열리는 기능)은 냄새·물기 제거에 확실히 도움 된다.디자인과 설치도 만족스럽다.주방 가구에 자연스럽게 녹아들고, 내부 랙 배열도 식기 넣고 빼기 편하게 설계되어 있다. 바구니 높낮이 조절이 돼서 큰 냄비나 접시도 수월하게 들어간다.소음은 손세척과 비교할 수는 없지만, 주방에서 조용한 편이라 가족 활동 시간에도 거슬리지 않는다.

Sentence (English): The design perfectly complemented my kitchen interior, and I was immediately drawn to it.
Comments (English): The design perfectly complemented my kitchen interior, and I was immediately drawn to it. True to its Objet Collection roots, the colors are truly luxurious, and it blends seamlessly with the kitchen cabinetry, leaving a clean, built-in feel. The dishwasher sits in the center of the kitchen without feeling overpowering. In fact, it adds a touch of sophistication to the kitchen. Guests are so impressed by its design that they often ask, "Is this a built-in dishwasher?" It's not just a beautiful design; its performance exceeds expectations. The most satisfying aspect, however, is its cleaning power. Thanks to the combined hot air and steam functions, even greasy frying pans and heavily seasoned dishes are thoroughly cleaned in one go. In the past, I had to pre-wash greasy dishes to feel safe, but now I can just put them in and they come out clean, which is incredibly convenient. I was particularly impressed by how well it removed stubborn stains, rice grime, and even soup stains. The drying function is also very satisfying. If dishes were still wet after washing, I'd have to wipe them again, which was a hassle. But with this product, thanks to the hot air drying, I rarely have to worry about moisture remaining. Even plastic containers dry relatively well, making it convenient to put away immediately after use. Hygiene is also a concern, and kitchen work has become much easier. The noise level exceeded my expectations. It's surprisingly quiet during operation, so it's not a major concern even in spaces close to the living room or kitchen. I love that it can be used at night without any time constraints, which is a huge plus. Being able to use it freely to fit my lifestyle is a huge plus. The biggest change, however, is the freedom from the stress of washing dishes. Reducing the number of times I had to wash dishes multiple times a day has given me more time to relax or do other things, which has definitely improved my quality of life. It also reduces the strain on my wrists and back, making it a truly successful choice in the long run. This product is completely satisfying, offering design, performance, and convenience. I confidently recommend it to anyone who values their kitchen decor but doesn't want to sacrifice practical performance, or who wants to reduce the stress of washing dishes. If you're considering a dishwasher, I believe you won't regret it.
Comments (Original): 주방 인테리어에 잘 어울리는 디자인이라 처음 보자마자 마음이 확 끌렸어요. 오브제컬렉션답게 색감이 정말 고급스럽고, 가전 특유의 튀는 느낌 없이 주방 가구와 자연스럽게 어우러져서 마치 빌트인 제품처럼 깔끔한 인상을 줍니다. 식기세척기가 주방 한가운데에 있어도 전혀 부담스럽지 않고, 오히려 주방 분위기를 한층 더 세련되게 만들어 주는 느낌이에요. 손님들이 와도 “이거 빌트인이에요?” 하고 물어볼 정도로 디자인 만족도가 큽니다.디자인만 예쁜 게 아니라 성능도 기대 이상이에요. 가장 만족스러운 부분은 역시 세척력입니다. 열풍과 스팀 기능이 함께 작동해서 그런지, 기름기 많은 프라이팬이나 양념이 진하게 남은 그릇들도 한 번에 말끔하게 세척됩니다. 예전에는 기름기 많은 그릇은 미리 애벌 설거지를 해야 마음이 놓였는데, 이제는 그럴 필요 없이 그대로 넣어도 깨끗하게 세척되어 나와서 정말 편해요. 특히 찌든 때나 밥풀, 국물 자국까지 깔끔하게 제거되는 점이 인상적이었습니다.건조 기능도 매우 만족스럽습니다. 세척 후에 그릇에 물기가 남아 있으면 다시 닦아야 해서 번거로운데, 이 제품은 열풍 건조 덕분에 물기 걱정이 거의 없어요. 플라스틱 용기까지도 비교적 잘 마르는 편이라 사용 후 바로 정리할 수 있어 편리합니다. 위생적인 부분에서도 안심이 되고, 주방 일이 한결 수월해졌어요.소음 부분도 기대 이상이었습니다. 작동 중에도 생각보다 조용해서 거실이나 주방과 가까운 공간에서도 크게 신경 쓰이지 않아요. 밤에 돌려도 부담이 없어서 시간에 구애받지 않고 사용할 수 있는 점이 정말 좋았습니다. 생활 패턴에 맞게 자유롭게 사용할 수 있다는 점이 큰 장점이에요.무엇보다 가장 큰 변화는 설거지 스트레스에서 해방되었다는 점이에요. 하루에도 몇 번씩 반복되던 설거지 시간이 줄어드니 여유가 생기고, 그 시간에 휴식을 취하거나 다른 일을 할 수 있어서 삶의 질이 확실히 올라간 걸 느낍니다. 손목이나 허리 부담도 줄어들어서 장기적으로 봐도 정말 잘한 선택이라는 생각이 들어요.디자인, 성능, 편의성까지 모두 만족스러운 제품입니다. 주방 인테리어를 중요하게 생각하면서도 실사용 성능을 놓치고 싶지 않은 분들, 설거지로 인한 스트레스를 줄이고 싶은 분들께 자신 있게 추천드리고 싶어요. 식기세척기를 고민 중이라면 후회 없는 선택이 될 거라고 생각합니다.

Sentence (English): First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household!
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.
