Sentence (English): The height adjustment is a huge plus.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): LG is the best choice for home appliances.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the automatic door opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I don't use them very often. Still, they're definitely useful features. Considering your environment and situation when comparing products will be a great help in making your decision. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I'm currently using the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I finally decided to upgrade my dishwasher.
Comments (English): I finally decided to upgrade my dishwasher. Stubborn rice? It all flies away. This is a revolution, this is my aunt. Thank you, LG. I would 200,000% buy again. I recommend LG to anyone I know who's considering a dishwasher. Sentence (English): For several months, I have struggled using my Bosch Series 100 Model SHE41CM6N dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Using my Bosch 100 Series SHE41CM6N/29 Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || For several months, I have struggled using my Bosch Series 100 Model SHE41CM6N dishwasher. Though it appears to be well made, the configuration of the racks is daunting. I struggle to find slots on the racks to accommodate my Corning ceramic dishware and an assortment of plastic tumblers. If you are able, you would be wise to take a sample of your dishes and tumblers to a showroom model and see if you can devise a strategy for loading the racks. Here are the problems that I experienced in placing my dishware on any rack: • Wire rack tines are grouped into different areas by the spacing between the tines. For example, some tine groups have narrow spacing and will accommodate only flat dinner plates but not cereal bowls. I quickly run out of spaces that fit a particular shape. I would have had almost no issues if most small spaces had been larger so most any size of dishware would fit. • A significant area of the upper rack is designed for large objects, such as pots. By design, that area is unable to securely hold small objects. If you generally have nothing large, this space is mostly unusable. Drinkware is cleaned in the upper rack, but there can be a major issue. I use plastic tumblers because they are lightweight, decorative, and thankfully break resistant. But these tumblers can bounce around while being washed and have been found sitting upright and filled to the brim with water. I needed to find a way to secure them; I now place an inverted wire basket on top of the tumblers and fasten this inverted “nest” to the dishwasher rack to immobilize them. Also, since the tumblers are plastic, they do not dry well, but this is common among some other dishwashers. • The bottom of the lower rack has large openings. It is impractical and maybe even unsafe to attempt to place small objects on them since they could shift under water pressure and fall through the rack onto the rotating sprinkler. • The plastic basket that holds utensils has 2 hinged covers, which have an array of holes for inserting the utensils and keeping them upright and separate. In my situation, almost all of my handles are too wide: my utensils will not insert through these holes; I must leave all the covers “open” and just clump the utensils in the compartments. Of course, small objects can be placed in any compartment, but an open cover would allow them to escape and bounce around the dishwasher. Unfortunately, each compartment does not have its own cover, so this problem is more extensive. (Note: you can solve this problem by buying a small stainless steel basket with a cover from online sources.) What happens when you dry metal utensils in a plastic basket? Answer: the plastic does not dry completely and the utensils it holds may be a little wet. A stainless steel basket for utensils could resolve the issue, but I have not found an equivalent one that fits this dishwasher model and that suits my budget. I continue to use my dishware (on extra dry and without a rinse aid). My ceramic plateware is dry and really shines. This dishwasher is pleasantly quieter than my old one. I hope this information helps you find a dishwasher that suits most all your needs.

I would have had almost no issues if most small spaces had been larger so most any size of dishware would fit. • A significant area of the upper rack is designed for large objects, such as pots. But these tumblers can bounce around while being washed and have been found sitting upright and filled to the brim with water. I needed to find a way to secure them; I now place an inverted wire basket on top of the tumblers and fasten this inverted “nest” to the dishwasher rack to immobilize them. It is impractical and maybe even unsafe to attempt to place small objects on them since they could shift under water pressure and fall through the rack onto the rotating sprinkler. • The plastic basket that holds utensils has 2 hinged covers, which have an array of holes for inserting the utensils and keeping them upright and separate. In my situation, almost all of my handles are too wide: my utensils will not insert through these holes; I must leave all the covers “open” and just clump the utensils in the compartments. Of course, small objects can be placed in any compartment, but an open cover would allow them to escape and bounce around the dishwasher. Unfortunately, each compartment does not have its own cover, so this problem is more extensive. Answer: the plastic does not dry completely and the utensils it holds may be a little wet. I continue to use my dishware (on extra dry and without a rinse aid). My ceramic plateware is dry and really shines. This dishwasher is pleasantly quieter than my old one. I hope this information helps you find a dishwasher that suits most all your needs.

Sentence (English): I'm so pissed off.
Comments (English): I'm so pissed off. I bought this because I was hooked on the "Bixby, open dishwasher door" feature, but after buying it, I spent hours searching the internet, deleting and reinstalling the dishwasher app from SmartThings, and repeating the process several times. However, it just kept endlessly repeating that Bixby couldn't perform that function, and the door wouldn't open. After the weekend, I called the service center to ask, and they said it doesn't work because it lacks the "Auto Open Door" feature. Then shouldn't it have stated that this model doesn't have the Auto Open Door feature, so the "Open Dishwasher Door" function won't work? If it was going to be like this, I would have paid more and bought a different model. I bought it hoping for more convenience with voice commands, but I feel like I paid my hard-earned money only to get swindled. I'm not an expert; how am I supposed to know if Bixby will open the door or not if that feature is actually present? I really don't like it. I left my old dishwasher behind because it had a nice design, upgraded features, and a discount, so I was happy to buy this, but it just annoys me every time I look at it. Seriously. Ugh. I get so angry every time I see it. I've already used it, so there's nothing I can do about it. To put it bluntly, I just want to throw it away. The dishwasher used to be one of the appliances I didn't like, but now it's become one of the ones I really don't like. I regret the time I spent agonizing over buying it for days.
