Sentence (English): Maybe I was my fault or I missed it in the product description, but when I removed the packaging I found out that this model had an outlet plug and required a receptacle.
Comments (English): Maybe I was my fault or I missed it in the product description, but when I removed the packaging I found out that this model had an outlet plug and required a receptacle. My previous 6 year old GE model was hard wired. So I had to get to the store and purchase an outlet box and a receptacle to install inside the sink cabinet. Ok done, now I was getting excited to hook it up. The instructions stated to hand tighten he water supply line only - when I turned on the dishwasher the line popped loose and I had a flood in my kitchen. I am 68, so maybe I did not do it strong enough, but after the cleanup, my daughter reconnected the supply line a nd it stayed tight when I turned on the machine. I like that it washes and dries much hotter than my GE I had.The little indentations on the Borns of most cups however still have water leftover after the wash.I am still getting used to the rack placements, I have had it now 2 1/2 weeks. The reason I did not give a 5 star rating was, that the flatware rack feels really cheap and flimsy and is rather small. For a $2,000 appliance I would have expected a sturdier rack for my flatware.

There is an auto feature that is supposed to detect the level of intensity needed to clean the dishes. LG suggests simply removing large particles of food and not rinsing the dishes. I was not believing that but surprisingly dirty dishes and a pasta pot came out sparkling clean and dry. The second rack easily adjust up and down and is a handy feature. I've used the third rack some and it can be helpful for serving spoons and other rather flat utensils. Overall, I am 100% happy with this dishwasher. I cannot speak of longevity since we have only had it a short time. We paid $550 for this and felt it was fairly priced and a good value.

Sentence (English): Every evening, I had to wash dishes and bottles.
Comments (English): [ My daily life has changed ] || ---------------- || Every evening, I had to wash dishes and bottles. Standing for over an hour, sometimes two, to do the dishes was exhausting. It was exhausting, especially while caring for my child. Waiting for my husband, who was always late, meant washing dishes late at night. My prejudice that dishwashers were only available in large sizes meant they were built-in, and I thought I couldn't use them in my rented apartment. But I realized I needed a stand dishwasher, so I searched and found this amazing information: a desktop dishwasher for six people. That's when I started studying (comparing products). After several days of searching, I stumbled upon actor Ha*'s YouTube video. I don't want to share any details, so just for reference. My heart was set on Mydia. The crucial point was that the layout of our house absolutely made a built-in dishwasher impossible. I needed a desktop dishwasher, but it was right in front of the gas stove. It was the worst possible situation. With only this much space, I searched again to find a size that would fit. I compared products from the Sam* and Ku* ranges. The only one with a two-tier design that had a water jet was the Mydia. I was always tired of washing dishes and bottles every evening. High-temperature washing, high-temperature drying, and UV sterilization were perfect for bottle washing! So I thought, "Ah! This is it!" After ordering, I received an installation date based on the information provided. The technician arrived on time! The installation was quick and easy! They followed my instructions and did a perfect job. The cords were neatly organized, so I was very satisfied. Loading dishes was a bit of a struggle when I first used it, but after a few months of use, I'm very satisfied and can load them all up easily. I can even use the dishwasher and spend time with my baby. My quality of life has greatly improved. We're a family of five, including the baby, but we're using it perfectly for six people. In the evening, I focus on dishes, and in the morning, I focus on bottles. Then, on days when there's a lot of dishes left during the day, I even use it for lunch. I'm very satisfied! Sentence (English): I'm a little sorry I decided on this dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ A little disappointed ] || ---------------- || I'm a little sorry I decided on this dishwasher. There was a promotion where you could get up to €100 back in cash. Despite being told in the store that I was entitled to it, I didn't get anything. As for the appliance itself, it really doesn't have much space and doesn't have a short 30-minute program. It washes and dries great, but I think that a cheaper competitor would have more space and wash just as well.
Comments (Original): [ Kar malo razočaran ] || ---------------- || Malo mi je žal,da sem se odločil za ta pomivalni stroj.Bila je akcija,da dobiš povrnjeno do 100€ kupnine. Kljub temu,da mi je bilo rečeno v trgovini,da mi pripada nisem dobil nič.Kar se pa samega aparata tiče pa ima res bolj malo prostora nima kratkega 30min.programa.Drugače pomije pa posuši super ampak mislim,da bi bilo pri konkurenci ceneje več prostora ter ravno tako dobro pomito.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher is really good, but unfortunately we overlooked that it is delivered without a front and base panel.
Comments (English): [ Excellent cleaning, but important parts missing ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is really good, but unfortunately we overlooked that it is delivered without a front and base panel. This was stated in the headline at Punkt1, but all product images showed the machine with a front and panel, which was misleading. At Bosch, however, it is clear from the images, but only upon close reading, that these parts are not included. We bought the machine because it was voted “best in test” by Tænk. The cleaning itself is excellent: The machine is extremely quiet and washes significantly better than our previous LG. However, the door slams very hard until a heavy kitchen door or an expensive metal door (approx. DKK 1,800) is installed, and you have to watch your fingers. At a price of DKK 12,698, I think that the front and base panel should be included. When these are purchased, the price ends up at approx. DKK 14,798. Therefore, the product is deducted two stars – otherwise it would get 5. Point 1 also connected the first machine incorrectly (high current), and the next one has an E31 error with water leakage. This is still being investigated and does not affect my rating.
Comments (Original): [ Fremragende rengøring, men vigtige dele mangler ] || ---------------- || Opvaskemaskinen er rigtig god, men vi overså desværre, at den leveres uden front og fodpanel. Det stod i overskriften hosPunkt1, men alle produktbilleder viste maskinen med front og panel, hvilket var misvisende. Hos Bosch fremgår det dog i billederne men kun ved nærlæsning, at disse dele ikke medfølger. Vi købte maskinen, fordi den er kåret “bedst i test” af Tænk. Selve rengøringen er fremragende: Maskinen er ekstremt støjsvag og vasker markant bedre end vores tidligere LG. Døren smækker dog meget hårdt i, indtil der monteres en tung køkkenlåge eller en dyr metaldør (ca. 1.800 kr.), og man skal passe på fingrene. Til en pris på 12.698 kr. mener jeg, at front og fodpanel burde medfølge. Når disse tilkøbes, ender prisen på ca. 14.798 kr. Derfor trækker produktet to stjerner ned – ellers ville den få 5.Punkt1tilsluttede desuden den første maskine forkert (stærkstrøm), og den næste har fået E31-fejl med vandlækage. Det undersøges stadig og påvirker ikke min vurdering.

Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Looks Great. Cleans Very Well. ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) Asthetically, this is a great-looking built-in dishwasher. The performance is great too (cleans perfectly and quiet - just like I expected it to be). I was pleasantly surprised to see that a red light comes on (projects onto the floor, just in front of the dishwasher kickplate) while the dishwasher is turned on. Great little feature! I am disappointed with the design of the two utensil holders. There are very limited places within the dishwasher where they can hang and most of the slots within the holders are too small and awkward. The touch-screen control panel (located at the top of the dishwasher door) is too sensitive. It turns on, beeps and/or reacts with a chime when I'm closing the door after loading a dish or two. I was further disappointed that the detergent samples that Bosh included with the dishwasher expired in 2023, over 2 1/2 years after I received my appliance. Overall, the 100 Plus Bosch Built-in Dishwasher is a great value for a well-known brand of dishwasher. I am happy with my choice.

Comments (English): [ Terrible Product- Leaks Immediately ] || ---------------- || If I could give this 0 stars I would, we bought this unit brand new and after 2 months it started leaking. So unless you enjoy handwashing everything you own and would like to have a $2,000 'statement piece' that sits empty and unused in your kitchen, I would stay away from this dishwasher.

For that reason, I'll probably avoid buying major appliances from Home Depot in the future.

Sentence (English): This replaced our GE dishwasher that gave up the ghost after 7.5 years.
Comments (English): This replaced our GE dishwasher that gave up the ghost after 7.5 years. This is the first LG appliance we've owned, so I'm hoping it will last longer than the GE. As an aside, we've had trouble with the GE refrigerator purchased at the same time as the GE dishwasher, so I'd never purchase another GE appliance.Having only had this for a month, it seems to do an adequate job of cleaning the dishes, however, because we only run it every 3 or so days, we rinse the dishes well before loading them into the dishwasher. Not sure of the performance if the dishes had a lot of dried on food.The lower and middle racks don't accommodate our mix of dishes and cookware as well as the old GE dishwasher. So, we've had to move things around and "reload" on occasion to fill it to capacity before running. This, unfortunately, is something I guess one can't really know until after purchase and use.The top (third) rack is of limited usefulness, at least for us.A bit disappointed in the delivery. One of the guys had mud on his boots (it was a rainy day) and tracked it into our home. In addition, they did not unbox the dishwasher and simply sat the unopened box in front of the opening in the cabinets.

Sentence (English): The dishwasher's door handle is made of plastic and, with normal repeated use, develops cracks and eventually fails.
Comments (English): [ Would be great if it didn't have a serious design flaw ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher's door handle is made of plastic and, with normal repeated use, develops cracks and eventually fails. When it breaks, it leaves a jagged plastic edge that can catch a passing person and cut them. There are reports on the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) of users being cut by this failure, and a quick online search shows many similar cases of the handle breaking in the exact same location and manner.This failure has happened to me twice. The first time occurred while the unit was under warranty. KitchenAid initially classified the issue as “cosmetic” and denied coverage. I had to argue that the broken handle was a safety concern—especially with children in the household—before they agreed to replace it under warranty.After the first repair, we were extremely careful in how we opened the dishwasher, always placing our hand fully at the top of the handle to better distribute force. Despite this, the handle failed again in the same way and in the same location.At that point, the dishwasher was out of warranty, and KitchenAid declined to help further. Unfortunately, the handle cannot be replaced on its own; it requires replacing the entire front panel, which costs approximately $300. I was unwilling to spend that amount on a part that appears likely to fail again as there has been no fix to the problem.I asked KitchenAid whether there were any alternative solutions, such as a redesigned or reinforced part. After repeated follow-ups, they offered a very small discount on a new dishwasher, but I would be responsible for installation costs. This made the offer less competitive than purchasing a new unit elsewhere during a promotion that included free installation. When I pointed this out, they declined to negotiate further.Overall, I am disappointed in GE (the maker of KitchenAid). Given the number of documented failures, this appears to be a known design issue, yet there is no permanent fix or meaningful support once the warranty expires. At a minimum, I would have expected a redesigned replacement part that eliminates the hazard.Based on this experience, I will likely look to other manufacturers in the future.

Sentence (English): Selected this Maytag dishwasher to replace a unit several years old.
Comments (English): Selected this Maytag dishwasher to replace a unit several years old. This washer does an outstanding job of cleaning dishes. It is very quiet during operation. It has 2 dry cycles to chose from to insure your dishes get dry after washing. Control panel is easy to understand and use. I installed this unit myself which is a moderately involved DIY project with just a few basic tools and the water line and power cord purchased separately. Overall very pleased with this dishwasher. It incudes a 1Y warranty for parts and labor as well as a 10 year warranty on racks, tub, and door seals. It also has a powerboost cycle for really dirty dishes or hard to remove food stuff.

Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher has very long cleaning cycles ] || ---------------- || I haven't bought a dishwasher in a long time, so I was curious what features I would be getting. For one thing, most appliances have far too many options, making choice overload a very real thing. Once I had this one installed and running, I was surprised at how quiet it was. I could no longer use sound cues coming in from the kitchen to tell me when the cycle was complete. My biggest issue (after canvasssing friends, I guess this issue is common) was the length of a 'normal' wash. No heat, no sanitizing, nothing extra. The cycle was 2 hours long. I have no idea what's going on in there, but two hours is a very long time to basically power rinse some dishes and glassware. I can run the "quick" mode, but that one is about an hour. The length of time these cycles run is not a bug, apparently, but it sure does surprise those who are used to far shorter cycles.

Sentence (English): Buy literally any other dishwasher from any other retailer available.
Comments (English): Buy literally any other dishwasher from any other retailer available. The "Sale" price on this dishwasher is a trap so that Home Depot and GE can unload faulty “lemon” appliances on the unsuspecting public. I recently purchased this dishwasher during a Black Friday sale and we have had nothing but issues. It all started when the installers for Home Depot dented the front of the stainless steel door while installing. They took a photo of the damage and told us to reach out to Home Depot to have them replace the unit. When we called about the dent and a replacement, Home Depot seemed unusually quick to offer us a discount on the unit to avoid needing to process a replacement. At the time we didn't think anything of it, but as the other issues started happening it made sense because once we accepted that discount, there was no way for us to return it, the 48hr return period for Home Depot had passed and we were now stuck with it and according to Home Depot, we were now “outside of their 48hr replacement window”. After the installers left, I went back and looked through the owners manual/Installation guide to find that many of the installation steps were skipped by the installer. Item was not leveled, plastic and styrofoam were left inside of it and they never ran a test wash as instructed. They were more interested in moving on to the next install and getting home early, instead of doing the install correctly. We were able to run it 2 times before it started leaking water everywhere and melting its own components. As shown by many of the other 1 star reviews on this appliance, the bottom sprayer arm got stuck against the dryer heating element and melted. That caused water to spray out of the front of the unit every time the arm rotated during the wash cycle. We reached out to Home Depot and they were the opposite of helpful. Instead of putting us in touch with the GE warranty department like they should have they booked the wrong service technician to come out, which set us back over a week and put us past GE's 7 day faulty appliance replacement policy. After we got in touch with the GE warranty department they scheduled us for a technician. When the technician arrives, he took one look at the issue and said “I have been seeing this a lot, it's a cheaply made appliance. You should've purchased a Bosch.” He ordered up a replacement sprayer arm as well as a new door seal for the leaking. When he came back over a week later to install the new sprayer arm and door seal, he ran a test cycle only to find out the unit is still leaking. Now the technician has stated that the whole front door needs be replaced on the unit. The "Sale" price on this dishwasher is a trap so that Home Depot and GE can unload faulty “lemon” appliances on the unsuspecting public. I recently purchased this dishwasher during a Black Friday sale and we have had nothing but issues. It all started when the installers for Home Depot dented the front of the stainless steel door while installing. They took a photo of the damage and told us to reach out to Home Depot to have them replace the unit. When we called about the dent and a replacement, Home Depot seemed unusually quick to offer us a discount on the unit to avoid needing to process a replacement. At the time we didn't think anything of it, but as the other issues started happening it made sense because once we accepted that discount, there was no way for us to return it, the 48hr return period for Home Depot had passed and we were now stuck with it and according to Home Depot, we were now “outside of their 48hr replacement window”. After the installers left, I went back and looked through the owners manual/Installation guide to find that many of the installation steps were skipped by the installer. Item was not leveled, plastic and styrofoam were left inside of it and they never ran a test wash as instructed. They were more interested in moving on to the next install and getting home early, instead of doing the install correctly. We were able to run it 2 times before it started leaking water everywhere and melting its own components. As shown by many of the other 1 star reviews on this appliance, the bottom sprayer arm got stuck against the dryer heating element and melted. That caused water to spray out of the front of the unit every time the arm rotated during the wash cycle. We reached out to Home Depot and they were the opposite of helpful. Instead of putting us in touch with the GE warranty department like they should have they booked the wrong service technician to come out, which set us back over a week and put us past GE's 7 day faulty appliance replacement policy. After we got in touch with the GE warranty department they scheduled us for a technician. When the technician arrives, he took one look at the issue and said “I have been seeing this a lot, it's a cheaply made appliance. You should've purchased a Bosch.” He ordered up a replacement sprayer arm as well as a new door seal for the leaking. When he came back over a week later to install the new sprayer arm and door seal, he ran a test cycle only to find out the unit is still leaking. Now the technician has stated that the whole front door needs be replaced on the unit. When I asked the technician sent by GE about when we should expect to have a working dishwasher, he said “I didn't say your dishwasher wasn't working, just put a large container underneath the front to catch the leak.” Wow, just wow. At the time or writing this review, which Home Depot sent me an email requesting I do so, we have been without a working dishwasher for over month and I have little faith at this point that I will have a working dishwasher anytime soon. Based on some of the other reviews here, even if it gets fixed It'll completely die out in a few years and we'll be back in this same situation, except this time having to pay out of pocket for all this. It feels like I'm in the Spiderman meme and Home Depot, GE and their various 3rd party service technicians and installers are all just pointing fingers at each other, with no one taking responsibility. GE makes a faulty appliance, Home Depot continues to sell these faulty appliances and all the installers/service technicians seem to know that the appliances are faulty… Yet no one mentions that to the customer until its too late. These dishwashers need to be recalled! Again, if you've made it this far in my review, I repeat, DO NOT BUY THIS OR ANY OTHER GE APPLIANCE FROM HOME DEPOT. The “Sale”price is not a deal, it's bait to get you to buy into this scam.

Sentence (English): This replaced our GE dishwasher that gave up the ghost after 7.5 years.
Comments (English): This replaced our GE dishwasher that gave up the ghost after 7.5 years. This is the first LG appliance we've owned, so I'm hoping it will last longer than the GE. As an aside, we've had trouble with the GE refrigerator purchased at the same time as the GE dishwasher, so I'd never purchase another GE appliance. Having only had this for a month, it seems to do an adequate job of cleaning the dishes, however, because we only run it every 3 or so days, we rinse the dishes well before loading them into the dishwasher. Not sure of the performance if the dishes had a lot of dried on food. The lower and middle racks don't accommodate our mix of dishes and cookware as well as the old GE dishwasher. So, we've had to move things around and "reload" on occasion to fill it to capacity before running. This, unfortunately, is something I guess one can't really know until after purchase and use. The top (third) rack is of limited usefulness, at least for us. A bit disappointed in the delivery. One of the guys had mud on his boots (it was a rainy day) and tracked it into our home. In addition, they did not unbox the dishwasher and simply sat the unopened box in front of the opening in the cabinets.

The Bosch had a 3rd rack, but it was shorter and I also didn't like that the Bosch cut the utensil bin on the lower rack to half the size; this Kitchenaid model has the full lower utensil bin.  My only complaint on this model is the running time...over 3 hours for a normal load.  However, I'm finding that I'm running the dishwasher less times/week because it holds more dishes per load, and it cleans really well so I don't end up putting some dishes back for a second run. I recommend it!
